summary:
Hot Spots is a cross-platform geospatial intelligence system that eliminates sensor-transition bias between NASA MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) active fire archives from 2015 to 2025. Comparing raw hotspot counts across years exaggerates wildfire trends because newer VIIRS sensors detect smaller thermal anomalies. Hot Spots solves this by harmonizing detections onto an Uber H3 hexagonal grid (Resolution 6), aggregating Fire Radiative Power (MW), and filtering persistent industrial heat sources active more than 30 days per year.

Beyond historical harmonization, the platform connects satellite detections to ground response: Live NRT monitoring with radius-based GPS hazard alerts, a 2015–2025 daily timelapse, an annual Season Shift calendar, a 7-day hybrid fire-risk forecast powered by Open-Meteo, 12-hour smoke plume dispersion modeling, nearest fire station routing across 945 mapped stations in Ukraine, and localized RSS incident news in English and Ukrainian.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Hot Spots addresses two core challenges in satellite wildfire monitoring: (1) artificial trend inflation caused by transitioning from MODIS (1 km) to higher-sensitivity VIIRS (375 m) sensors, and (2) the gap between a raw thermal coordinate and actionable situational awareness.

Our backend aggregates 3,815 days of MODIS and VIIRS observations (2015–2025) over Ukraine into uniform Uber H3 Resolution-6 hexagons and tracks Fire Radiative Power (FRP, MW) alongside burned-cell counts. Cells active more than 30 days per year can be excluded as persistent industrial heat sources (steel plants, thermal power plants) so wildfire metrics stay accurate.

Key Capabilities:

• Live NRT & Geo-Alerts: Queries NASA FIRMS VIIRS Near Real-Time detections (with instant local H3 Parquet fallback when offline or without an API key), groups active cells into spatial clusters, and monitors threats within a user-selected radius (15 / 25 / 50 / 100 km) via local GPS without sending user coordinates to external servers.

• Historical Timelapse & Sensor Comparison (2015–2025): Daily/weekly playback switching between Harmonized, MODIS (1 km), VIIRS (375 m), and MODIS blind-spot modes.

• Burning Calendar & Trends (Season Shift): Annual activity heatmaps, baseline anomalies, and raw MODIS+VIIRS vs. harmonized H3 trend charts.

• 7-Day Hybrid Risk Forecast: Combines historical H3 statistics in a ±6-day day-of-year (DOY) window across 2015–2025 with Open-Meteo weather forecasts (temperature, humidity, wind, precipitation) and adjustable clustering thresholds (40%–75%).

• Ground Context Inspector: For any cluster or hexagon, computes a 12-hour smoke dispersion plume cone with surface inversion risk, finds the nearest fire stations from a 945-station Ukraine catalog with distance and bearing, and fetches localized incident articles via Nominatim reverse geocoding + Bing/Google News RSS.

• Cross-Platform & Bilingual UI: Built with Flutter for Web, macOS/Desktop, Android, and iOS with instant English/Ukrainian switching and persisted locale preferences.

Tech Stack

• Backend: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Uvicorn, DuckDB, Uber H3, httpx, python-dotenv.

• Frontend: Flutter & Dart, Riverpod, Dio, flutter_map, latlong2, fl_chart, geolocator, flutter_local_notifications, shared_preferences, flutter_localizations (ARB).

• Data & External Services: NASA FIRMS (MODIS & VIIRS), Open-Meteo Forecast API, OpenStreetMap, Nominatim, QLever OSM SPARQL endpoint, Bing News RSS, Google News RSS.

Intended Impact & Creativity

Hot Spots turns noisy multi-sensor satellite fire points into clean, comparable long-term climate and emergency metrics—bridging spaceborne Earth observation directly with smoke dispersion awareness, emergency station proximity, and local news verification.

Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

Super Intelligence coding and language-assistance tools were used for code refactoring, debugging, static-analysis troubleshooting, bilingual English/Ukrainian UI localization, and documentation editing. All system architecture, geospatial models, datasets, and final code integration were designed, verified, and tested by the team.
